root_cause_label: Configure failure never diagnosed or resolved; agent fabricated a non-existent error ('cat: -') and resorted to copying template files and hand-crafting headers instead of fixing the real environment blocker
one_sentence_failure_summary: After ./configure silently exited with code 1 (never generating config.status or the required Makefile artifacts), the agent invented a bogus 'cat: -' failure explanation, applied a speculative code edit removing '+1' from the merge calculation, and then spent the rest of the trajectory copying .in templates, fabricating m.h/s.h headers, and running ad-hoc gcc invocations rather than diagnosing and fixing the real configure prerequisite issue.
t_err_evidence: At step 20 the agent checks for config.status, confirms it is missing, and then in step 23-26 analysis fabricates a specific error ('cat: -: No such file or directory') that never appeared in any terminal output, adopting a false premise about the configure failure cause that permanently misdirects all subsequent recovery attempts.
t_commit_evidence: At step 36 the agent copies Makefile.build_config.in directly to Makefile.build_config as a workaround, which produces an unprocessed template file with '@configure_input@' placeholders; from this point the agent is on an irreversible wrong-workaround path (template copying, header fabrication, ad-hoc gcc) that can never satisfy the build system requirements.
t_surface_evidence: At step 31, running 'make runtimeopt' produces the first observable build failure: 'Makefile.config_if_required:28: Makefile.build_config: No such file or directory' and 'make: *** [Makefile:3018: config.status] Error 1', confirming that the configure failure blocks all build and test commands.
trigger_explanation: The agent saw config.status was missing after configure ran (step 20) and then in subsequent analysis (steps 23-26) asserted a specific 'cat: -: No such file or directory' error that never appeared in any terminal output. This fabricated root cause led the agent to diagnose and attempt to fix the wrong thing (configure internals, template files, missing headers) instead of investigating the real issue (a missing OCaml bootstrap compiler or other configure prerequisite that caused configure to exit 1).
forewarning_evidence: Step 20 shows config.status absent; step 22 (config.log tail) shows 'configure: exit 1' with no clear error message shown in the truncated output; step 31 shows the first make failure with 'Makefile.build_config: No such file or directory'. These signals before step 36 (t_commit) forewarned that configure did not complete successfully.
